draft.title: Protons, neutrons and electrons
card: the smallest part of an element that still has the properties of that element.
a particle with a positive charge. It sits in the nucleus, the small centre of the atom.
a particle with no charge. It also sits in the nucleus.
a particle with a negative charge. It moves around the nucleus and is far lighter than a proton or neutron.
draft.remember: An atom is the smallest part of an element. The nucleus holds the positive protons and the neutral neutrons. The light, negative electrons move around it.

a.q: Which two types of particle make up the nucleus of an atom?
a.why: Protons and neutrons are the heavier particles that sit in the nucleus. Protons and electrons can seem right because both have a charge, but electrons move around the nucleus rather than sitting in it.
a.clue: Go through the three particles and recall where each one is.

b.q: A neutral sodium atom has 11 protons. How many electrons does it have, and what is the reason?
opts: 11, because electrons sit in the nucleus
12, so there is one more than the protons
0, because the atom has no overall charge
b.why: A neutral atom has equal numbers of positive protons and negative electrons, so 11 electrons cancel the charge of 11 protons. No overall charge does not mean no electrons, because the charges balance.
b.clue: Neutral means the positive and negative charges are balanced.

problems.detail: The card never says that a proton and an electron carry equal and opposite charges, or that a neutral atom has equal numbers of protons and electrons. Students need that idea to answer, and only the clue supplies part of it. The card should add a line that a neutral atom has as many electrons as protons, so the charges balance.

proposal.title: Protons, neutrons and electrons
card: An atom is the smallest part of an element that still has the properties of that element. At its centre is a tiny core called the nucleus.
The nucleus holds protons, which have a positive charge, and neutrons, which have no charge.
Electrons have a negative charge. They move around the nucleus and are far lighter than protons or neutrons.
A proton and an electron carry equal and opposite charges. A neutral atom has as many electrons as protons, so the charges cancel out.
proposal.remember: Positive protons and neutral neutrons sit in the nucleus. Negative electrons move around it, matching the protons in a neutral atom.

b.clue: Neutral means the positive and negative charges are balanced.
